findings.title: Unsupported nested MSBuild declarations can validate a NuGet lock owner and create a false framework fact
affected_requirement: specs/002-language-framework-detection/contracts/framework-detection.md:82-86 requires the sole NuGet lock owner to use the supported direct-manifest shape with literal, unconditional ownership declarations.
specs/002-language-framework-detection/contracts/framework-detection.md:154-157 requires rejection coverage for unsupported and conditional/dynamic owners.

evidence.detail: ValidateNuGetOwnerManifest searches every same-namespace descendant PackageReference or FrameworkReference. It does not require the declaration to be a child of a project-level ItemGroup and does not reject declarations nested beneath Target, Choose, When, or another unsupported MSBuild execution construct.

The direct evidence parser correctly consumes only project-level ItemGroup children. The owner validator therefore accepts a broader and unsafe syntax than the detector's supported direct-manifest grammar.

Owner-negative coverage exercises malformed roots, unsupported roots, explicit Condition attributes, dynamic SDK values, unsafe paths, oversize files, and multiple candidates, but does not cover a literal PackageReference or FrameworkReference nested under Target or Choose.

findings.reproduction_reasoning: A sole same-root owner such as <Project><Target Name="Late"><ItemGroup><PackageReference Include="Example.Unmatched" /></ItemGroup></Target></Project> has no supported project-level ownership declaration. Nevertheless, lines 1128-1139 classify it ParsedSupported because the nested declaration is literal and has no Condition attribute. A matched packages.lock.json is then eligible and can produce a Medium framework fact for an applicable Code Unit.
findings.impact: A committed lock file can be associated with a scope through an unsupported, execution-dependent MSBuild construct. This bypasses the validated-owner seam and permits an incorrect persisted framework fact.
findings.correction_outcome: Make NuGet owner validation consume exactly the supported project-level grammar used by direct detection: the root SDK attribute, direct Project/Sdk elements, and PackageReference or FrameworkReference elements directly beneath project-level ItemGroup elements. Declarations beneath Target, Choose, When, Import-driven, or other unsupported structures must not prove ownership. Add observed RED/GREEN cases for Target-nested and Choose/When-nested declarations paired with a matched lock; require no Medium fact, one bounded closed audit without raw values, continued independent valid evidence, and preserved valid project-level owner behavior.

planned_change_authorization.trigger: The correction materially changes Scan parsing and lock-owner filtering behavior.
planned_change_authorization.required_action: Before task generation, obtain explicit user approval identifying this Scan-strategy trigger, the exact owner-grammar correction, its effects, implementation intent, and affected plan and PRD material. The approval does not waive TDD, both Full review axes, E2E, security, or verification.

quality_assessment.security_and_redaction: The QR8 namespace-spoofing and bounded-inventory corrections are sound, fail closed, and retain bounded diagnostics. QR9-001 remains a High data-integrity defect.
quality_assessment.edge_cases: REVISE because unsupported nested MSBuild ownership structures are not rejected.
quality_assessment.test_quality: QR8 coverage is substantial for foreign namespaces, pinned object identity, output and retained-record overflow, cancellation, and independent artifact continuation. NuGet owner tests omit the unsupported nested-execution shape that exposes QR9-001.
quality_assessment.architecture_seams: Layering and the committed-snapshot seam remain sound. The direct-parser and lock-owner-validator grammars are inconsistent.
quality_assessment.regression_risk: High until QR9-001 receives authorized RED-GREEN correction and both Full review axes are regenerated.
quality_assessment.forbidden_scope: No Worker Agent/tool, orchestration, dispatch, scheduling, retry, PRD weakening, document generation, persistence-schema, API, or UI expansion was found.

summary: REVISE. The QR8 namespace and inventory findings are corrected, but QR9-001 is a new High correctness and data-integrity finding: NuGet lock ownership accepts unsupported nested MSBuild declarations and can create a false Medium framework fact.
